{{short description|Two properties of polynomial roots}}
{{format footnotes |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Hudde's rules''' are two [[properties of polynomial roots]] described by [[Johann Hudde]].

# <p>If <var>r</var> is a [[double root]] of the polynomial equation <!--
--><math display="block">a_0x^n + a_1x^{n-1} + \cdots + a_{n-1}x + a_n = 0 </math> <!--
-->and if <math>b_0, b_1, \dots, b_{n-1}, b_n</math> are numbers in [[arithmetic progression]], then <var>r</var> is also a [[root]] of <!--
--><math display="block">a_0b_0x^n + a_1b_1x^{n-1} + \cdots + a_{n-1}b_{n-1}x + a_nb_n = 0. </math> <!--
-->This definition is a form of the modern [[theorem]] that if <var>r</var> is a double root of ''ƒ''(<var>x</var>)&nbsp;=&nbsp;0, then <var>r</var> is a root of ''ƒ''<nowiki>&nbsp;'</nowiki>(<var>x</var>)&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.</p>
# <p>If for <var>x</var>&nbsp;=&nbsp;<var>a</var> the polynomial <!--
--><math display="block">a_0x^n + a_1x^{n-1} + \cdots + a_{n-1}x + a_n </math> <!--
-->takes on a relative [[maximum]] or [[minimum]] [[Value (mathematics)|value]], then <var>a</var> is a root of the equation <!--
--><math display="block">na_0x^n + (n-1)a_1x^{n-1} + \cdots + 2a_{n-2}x^2 + a_{n-1}x = 0. </math> <!--
-->This definition is a modification of [[Fermat's theorem (stationary points)|Fermat's theorem]] in the form that if ''ƒ''(<var>a</var>) is a relative maximum or minimum value of a polynomial ''ƒ''(<var>x</var>), then ''ƒ''<nowiki>&nbsp;'</nowiki>(<var>a</var>)&nbsp;=&nbsp;0, where ''ƒ''<nowiki>&nbsp;'</nowiki> is the [[derivative]] of ''ƒ''.</p>

Hudde was working with [[Frans van Schooten]] on a [[Latin]] edition of [[La Géométrie]] of [[René Descartes]]. In the 1659 edition of the translation, Hudde contributed two letters: "Epistola prima de Redvctione Ǣqvationvm" (pages 406 to 506), and "Epistola secvnda de Maximus et Minimus" (pages 507 to 16). These letters may be read by the Internet Archive link below.
